Frequently Asked Questions

What is Re:Booth (Re:ブース), and how does it differ from a standard exhibition booth?

Standard wooden booths are dismantled and discarded after the exhibition—this is the usual premise. Re:Booth, on the contrary,an exhibition booth designed and built on the premise of “reuse for the next event.”It is.

It is composed of reusable materials—including the truss framework, display panels, display stands, floor panels, lighting, and sales‑negotiation fixtures. After the exhibition, we store the booth in our warehouse and re‑assemble it for the next show. Only consumables such as protective tape are discarded.

How does it differ from the so‑called “system booth”?

Conventional system booths rely on standardized panel combinations, limiting design flexibility and inevitably giving a prefabricated appearance.

Re:Booth does not use system panels as the primary structure,instead assembling the booth around a truss frameworkthereby securing greater shape flexibility. Moreover, the flooring uses reusable resin panels rather than disposable punch‑carpet that is discarded after each exhibition.

Won’t reusing the booth result in the same appearance each time?

It does not.What remains common isonly the framework and the fixtures

. The graphics, layout, and fixture arrangement can be redesigned for each exhibition. In fact, the same client has exhibited at different shows with different booth sizes, each time with a unique presentation.

Will the appearance suffer when using reused materials?

We inspect and maintain the materials in our warehouse after each exhibition, replacing any worn components. Graphics and floor panels that are visible to visitors are evaluated with top priority for condition.

How much does it cost? 815,350 yen (excluding tax) + transportation feeis the estimate (Pattern A with truss + display stand). For Pattern B without truss, it is 723,350 yen (excluding tax) + transportation fee.

The market price for a general woodwork booth is from 1.2 million yen per booth, and even a standard booth provided by the organizer is from 600,000 yen.

Does it become cheaper for the second time onwards?

Do costs decrease for the second and subsequent uses?Yes, they become cheaper. Because we reuse the already‑produced materials,will be the cost (1 booth, Pattern A. Approx. 180,000 yen / approx. 22% reduction compared to the first time).

The difference increases with more booths; for a 3-booth Pattern A, the cost is 1,695,590 yen for the first time, and 1,207,960 yen from the second time onwards (a reduction of approx. 490,000 yen).

What is included in the estimate?

What is included in the estimate?The package plan includes the following:It is.

  • Transportation fee is billed separately.
  • Planning and management (including perspective design) / truss / display stand kit
  • Electrical work / Floor panels / LED lighting
  • Electrical work / floor panels / LED lighting
  • Printed materials/outputs (5 x A1 panels + leaflets) / Management fee

On-site operation director (40,000 yen per person per day) and operation staff (25,000 yen per person per day) are optional.

What is the transportation fee?

What is the transportation cost?

  • Tokyo 160,000 yen
  • Nagoya 300,000 yen
  • Osaka 400,000 yen
  • Hiroshima 500,000 yen
  • Fukuoka 600,000 yen
Can you store the booth until the next trade show?

Can you store the booth until the next exhibition?Yes. The period until the next participationwill be kept in our warehouse

(two locations within Saitama). The client does not need to secure storage space or manage the materials.

Can the booth be used if the number of bays or layout changes for the next event?Yes. Because the booth is composed of modular truss and display‑stand units,it can be re‑configured to accommodate an increase or decrease in booth count.

Who owns the rights to the produced booth?

Who holds ownership of the produced booth?

The ownership of decorative items such as graphics belongs to the client. At the end of the exhibition, they can be handed over directly or stored in our warehouse. (If shipment is requested while stored, packing fees and delivery charges will apply.)

Items not listed above—including structural components such as trusses, framework, floor panels, chairs, tables, and AV equipment—are available for rental on a per‑use basis from us. Purchase is also possible; a separate quote will be provided upon request.

How far in advance should we consult?Please consult with us using this as a reference. The standard schedule is as follows.

  • 8 weeks prior: Order confirmation / Application to construction company
  • 7 weeks prior: Submission of first design draft
  • 6 weeks prior: Submission of second design draft
  • 5 weeks prior: Application for electrical work and delivery
  • 4 weeks prior: Design finalization / Creation of construction drawings
  • 2 weeks prior: Final proofreading and submission
  • Setup day: Final construction confirmation
  • 1 week after the exhibition period: Review meeting

Please note that we also have track records of production periods of 2 weeks or 1 month, so please consult with us even if your schedule is tight.

The application documents for the organizer are complicated and I am worried. Can you handle it on my behalf?

Yes, we will handleall exhibition procedures on your behalf. We will take custody of your login information for the exhibitor-only website, and our specialized staff will complete applications and submissions within the deadline and report the progress to you.

  • Booth construction / preparation related: Exhibitor pass application, rental decoration order, electrical trunk line work, floor work (anchoring), water piping, air supply, and others 12 types or more
  • Equipment / service related: Internet connection, rental PC, badge reader, AV equipment, transportation / courier, food service, and others 12 types or more
  • Safety / special applications: Bringing in dangerous goods, bringing in / using hydrogen, ceiling structure application, fire department application, interpreter arrangement, and others 10 types or more
Can you handle events anywhere in Japan? What about overseas?

Yes, we can. In addition to our Osaka Head Office and Tokyo Branch Office, we have sales offices in Sapporo, Nagoya, Hiroshima, Fukuoka, and Okinawa.

We have a track record at Tokyo Big Sight, Makuhari Messe, Pacifico Yokohama, Intex Osaka, Port Messe Nagoya, Aichi Sky Expo, Marine Messe Fukuoka, Okinawa Convention Center, Kyoto International Exhibition Hall Miyako Messe, Yonago Convention Center, and others.

Overseas, we are also handling exhibitions in Düsseldorf, Germany, and pavilions for the Osaka・Kansai Expo 2025 (including on-site meetings in English and various application agency services).

Can I also ask you to handle things other than the booth collectively?

Yes, you can. We provide a one-stop service including printed materials such as panels and leaflets, monitors/AV equipment, novelty item planning and arrangement, booth companion / booth MC arrangement, and even operation directors and operation staff during the exhibition period.

The only items customers need to prepare are their own company brochures and their own PCs.

How much CO2 can be reduced?

Based on a calculation compliant with ISO 14067:2018 assuming a 3-booth, 3-day event at Tokyo Big Sight,a 77% reduction compared to conventional disposable wooden boothshas been confirmed.

  • Total emissions per project: 91.7 kg-CO2e (conventional wooden booth 396.7 kg-CO2e / −305.0 kg)
  • Functional unit: 1.70 kg-CO2e/m²·day (conventional wooden booth 7.35 /−77%）
  • Disposal stage CO2: 0 kg (conventional wooden booth 223.7 kg / zero)
  • Raw material CO2: 57.4 kg (conventional wooden booth 148.8 kg / −60%)

56% of the emissions from conventional wooden booths originate from incinerating the wood after the exhibition period. Re:Booth achieves maximum reduction by 'not burning'.

Can I receive data that can be used for my company's sustainability reporting?

Yes.This can be directly used for reporting under Scope 3 Category 1 (Purchased goods and services). It will be provided in a format that can be submitted as supplier-specific data at the highest level of the Quality Pyramid for reporting to CDP, TCFD, SBTi, etc. We will also provide materials for comparative reports for internal and external use.

Are there any third-party evaluations or certifications?
  • Osaka City New Business Field Development Business Certification (Venture Procurement System) Certified — Certified for reasons including 'Utilization of reusable shared materials resulting in low environmental impact' and 'Superior design unlike general system booths'
  • 11th SDGs Business Seminar SDGs Business Hope Award Awarded — Judged based on three criteria: 'Sociality', 'Sustainability', and 'Business Viability'
  • Trademark Registration No. 6772061 — Registered on January 19, 2024 / Trademark holder: Orgiast Co., Ltd.
What is the estimated impact on the entire industry?

73.9% of all domestic exhibition booths are disposable wooden booths. If Re:Booth achieves a 50% market share,an annual waste reduction of 3,300 to 6,600 tons(equivalent to the annual waste disposal of a medium-sized town) is expected.

In which industries do you have a track record?

IT/DX, manufacturing/engineering, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics/beauty, real estate, human resources, food, logistics, government agencies/research institutes, overseas government pavilions, etc. We also have extensive track records with academic conference booths.

How does the design proposal process proceed?

After the initial consultation, the process proceeds on a schedule of order confirmation at 8 weeks prior, first draft at 7 weeks prior, second draft at 6 weeks prior, and finalization at 4 weeks prior. We also utilize generative AI for creating perspective drawings.
